scale.P0: Pilot blocker: a security or privacy defect, a legal obligation, or a state staff cannot get out of without SQL on the server.
scale.P1: Pilot operations: a pilot flow or a Docs/23 Must screen cannot be done in the console, or a server-side safety rule is missing; a console workaround may exist but is weak.
scale.P2: Completeness and efficiency: Docs/23 Should items, extra filters and context, aggregates; the console has a working workaround.
scale.P3: Tied to a later feature (the AI build).

complexity_scale.S: ~1 point: one read operation, or a field or filter on an existing operation.
complexity_scale.M: ~2-3 points: two or three operations, or one rule plus a scheduler job, or a new column with a migration.
complexity_scale.L: ~4-6 points: a new entity with its operations, or a rule that cuts across many operations.
complexity_scale.XL: 6+ points: a cross-module rewrite with per-module conflict rules.
complexity_scale.note: Points are relative effort per the backend definition of done (Docs/40 text, registry and codegen, handler, projection, sweep resolver, happy-path + authz-negative + rule tests). Reference: backend S12 (3 new operations, 2 changed, staff tooling, contract bump) is about 9 points.

method: Closed items (BR-01..BR-06) are kept for history only.
Each open item is rated by what goes wrong without it at the pilot, not by its source label (blocker/high/must/should): the source labels described when the console needed it.
Items whose parts differ in risk are split (BR-35 row vs filters vs more-info vs correction; BR-15 actions vs redaction; BR-21 list vs notification; BR-26 ids vs notice).
Console workarounds already built (deviations D-xx) lower the priority only when they are safe; they never lower a server-side safety or privacy rule.

principles: Order: first the reads that unblock the console (S13), then the pilot blockers (privacy S14, legal S15, staff keys S16), then pilot-operations completeness (S17-S19), then Should items (S20-S24), then closure (S25).

One stage = one working session that fits a 5-hour token window. Target load <= 11 points (backend S12 was about 9, S11 about 11). Security-sensitive or cross-module stages are planned lighter (S16, S22, S23).

A stage groups items by module and contract area so the session reads one set of docs and code (backend conventions.context_budget: read only the listed ranges, lean on the generated registry, copy patterns from finished modules).

Every stage follows the backend definition of done per operation and ends with contract:check and openapi:check green and the console contract regenerated, so the tree is never left with a half-updated registry.
If a session runs long, stop at the stage's split_point and move the rest to S25 or the named later stage; never split inside a task.

Stage-level unit and integration tests in lite mode stay part of each stage (they are development, not the test run). The strict cross-component runs (console and PWA E2E and test:int, R-10, R-13, R-20) wait for the whole-plan test run after S25 (PD-03). DQ-08 asks the owner to confirm this reading.
